title: I booked a $200 flight to Panama on a whim, then decided to move there. I found the community I was missing in the US.
summary:
This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Chrysten Crockett, a Cleveland native who moved from Atlanta to Panama City.
I went home that night, looked up Panama City, and I was like, "Oh wow, it's a big city.
I was blown away because I had never been, and I didn't know much about the country.
Crockett said she gets a lot more for her rent in Panama City than in the US.
As a solo woman traveler, when I first got here, I didn't know what the safety situation would be like.

title: Reform says it will prioritise British-born young workers for social housing
summary:
"We're saying that the first people we should be looking after are young, British workers - under 35, young British married couples, young British veterans - who have done the right thing," he said.
Rules would be changed to reserve at least half of all social homes in England for British-born workers aged under 35, with prioritisation also given to married couples, veterans, victims of domestic violence and care leavers.
Tice claimed there were currently 540,000 existing affordable social homes occupied by overseas nationals and he wanted that to change.
The Conservative Party, which also said it would revoke the right of foreign nationals to social housing, accused Reform of "trying to catch up" with its policies.
Sir James Cleverly, shadow housing secretary, added: "The Conservatives have already set out comprehensive plans to ensure British nationals are at the front of the queue for social housing.

title: He was waiting for his son to return from the USS Lincoln. Then Border Patrol arrested him.
summary:
Luis Manuel Aviles, 48, was arrested after leaving his house to take his car to the mechanic, according to his wife, Argelia Aviles.
Aviles' son said in a Facebook post that he has been working 12-hour work shifts for more than 250 days without a break on the USS Lincoln, which is deployed in the Middle East.
Joshua Aviles wrote in his post on Saturday that he was still on the USS Lincoln "fighting for a country that has given me everything" when he got a call about his father's detention on Saturday morning.
I don't know how I can mentally continue working 12+ hour days knowing that my dad is somewhere, possibly treated like a criminal," Joshua Aviles wrote.
When six months passed and his son didn't come back, Aviles was distraught, she said.

title: Trump administration's 75-country visa ban was illegal, judge rules
summary:
Trump administration's 75-country visa ban was illegal, judge rulestoggle caption David J. Phillip/APA federal judge has struck down a Trump administration ban on issuing immigrant visas to people from 75 countries, saying the policy violated federal immigration law by discriminating on the basis of nationality.
However, the Trump administration's policy banned certain people from receiving immigrant visas "based solely on their nationality," the judge wrote.
Vargas said the Trump administration's policy was "contrary to law" and exceeded the authority of Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
The judge's ruling vacated the visa ban and also set aside visa denials that were based only on the policy.
The ban was part of a broader effort by the Trump administration to limit legal and illegal immigration.

title: Tunisia recovers 11 bodies after boat carrying migrants sinks, 3 missing
summary:
The boat, believed to be headed towards Italy, set off on Thursday with 15 mostly young people on board.
The bodies of 11 people have been recovered while three others remain missing after a boat carrying migrants and asylum seekers sank off Tunisia, according to an official.
In July, 46 rights groups, including Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch, issued a joint statement criticising the EU’s 2023 deal with Tunisia to curb migration.
The International Organization for Migration estimated that more than 35,000 people have died or gone missing in the Mediterranean since 2014.
The Tunisian Observatory for Human Rights has previously estimated that about 10,000 Tunisians have gone missing at sea while trying to cross to Europe since 2011.

title: Two Dead, Twelve Missing as Migrant Boat Capsizes Off Tunisian Coast
summary:
TUNIS, Tunisia (AP) – A boat carrying migrants capsized off the coast of southern Tunisia, killing at least two people and leaving 12 missing, Tunisia’s national guard said Saturday.
A helicopter and coast guard boats were then dispatched to the area in search of more survivors, according to an Associated Press photojournalist at the scene.
Migrant departures from Tunisia have fallen sharply since the European Union and Tunisia signed a sweeping agreement in 2023.
It included EU funding and technical support for Tunisian border control and coast guard training to help Tunisia curb irregular migration and deter human traffickers in the Mediterranean basin.
In July, Amnesty International said EU support for border control in Tunisia continued to fuel serious rights violations.
